journey.question: What happens when a shopper asks for a refund?
journey.title: Refunds
journey.summary: A shopper asks for money back on a paid order. The API marks the order and queues a job, and the worker asks the payment provider to refund it.

nodes.label: Shop API
nodes.summary: The HTTP API that holds orders and the waiting jobs.

nodes.label: Worker
nodes.summary: The process that takes jobs from the API and talks to the provider.

nodes.label: Payment provider
nodes.summary: The third-party service that holds the charge and makes refunds.

anchor.before: // refund_pending here and the worker gives the money back.
anchor.after: // The worker reports how the charge or the refund went: 409 when the order was settled before.

nodes.label: startRefund
nodes.summary: Moves a paid order to refund_pending.

anchor.before: // was asked for already): two refund requests for one order start one refund.

nodes.label: JobQueue
nodes.summary: Adds a job to the in-memory queue.

anchor.after: // Removes and returns the oldest job, or null when none is waiting.

nodes.label: refundOrder (worker)
nodes.summary: Retries the refund call for one job.

steps.title: The request is checked before anything changes
steps.lead: The order must exist, belong to the caller, have a valid amount, and the queue must have room.

steps.title: The paid check sits inside the UPDATE
steps.lead: Only a row still paid is changed, and the number of changed rows tells the caller whether it won.

steps.title: The queue is a plain array in this process
steps.lead: Waiting jobs live only in this array, while the order's status lives in the database.

steps.title: Every attempt uses the same key, built from the order
steps.lead: The key is only the order id, so retries and any later refund of this order share it.

questions.text: What happens to an order in refund_pending if the API restarts before the worker takes its refund job?
After a failed refund, what happens when the customer asks again for a different amount, given the idempotency key?
Why does startRefund check the status inside its UPDATE instead of relying on the status read in refundOrder?
